takes.name: Cragwool
takes.brief: A sure-footed upland browser with tall muscular forequarters, a low sloping rump, four broad split gripping feet and a short wedge-shaped mammalian muzzle tucked close to the chest. Warm ivory clipped wool meets smooth charcoal callus plates on shins and lower sides; a short thick tail, no horns. It leans uphill with front feet higher than rear, clearly bearing weight.
takes.description: Cragwool tests a steep-ground browser with weight carried forward over broad gripping feet. Its compact muzzle and clipped wool contrast with the dark callused lower body; the grazing role and exact size remain proposals.

creator_review.notes: Liked Cragwool; make face modestly more predatory and less stub-nosed. Preserve body/coat.

takes.name: Reedstrider
takes.brief: An upright bipedal browser with two strong hind legs, two much smaller flexible feeding forelimbs, a heavy counterbalancing tail and a deep low pelvis. The compact head has soft mammalian lips and small upright ears, no beak or dinosaur snout. Smooth muted moss-green leathery body with a narrow cinnamon-fibre ridge along the shoulders; no pouch. Moving through knee-deep reeds with realistic forward momentum.
takes.description: Reedstrider proposes a tall floodplain browser whose tail balances a low pelvis and strong hind legs. A compact soft-lipped face and small feeding forelimbs give it a distinct rhythm of movement.

creator_review.notes: Liked Reedstrider; spread the copper mohawk-like fibre covering over the body, not only the back ridge.

takes.name: Shellshoulder
takes.brief: A long low four-legged amphibious mollusc hunter; powerful forelimbs brace a narrow torso while rear feet paddle and a short muscular oar tail drives water. Broad smooth head with two rounded crushing cheek bulges, small eyes set high, an ordinary closed mouth, no external gills. Dense blue-green pebbled skin transitions to ochre scutes over the shoulder joint only. No fur or feather mantle.
takes.description: Shellshoulder tests a heavy river-edge hunter built to brace and crush hard-shelled prey. Its dense skin, rounded cheeks and shoulder scutes create a different surface and silhouette from the furred animals.

creator_review.notes: Cut by creator; excluded from further references.

sheets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an ORIGINAL Breachline creature LINEUP plate, landscape 1536 x 1024, exactly SIX different whole animals in a clean THREE-COLUMN by TWO-ROW layout. Reading order: top-left 1, top-centre 2, top-right 3, bottom-left 4, bottom-centre 5, bottom-right 6. NO printed numbers, names, letters, panel borders, arrows, logo or signature. Each animal entirely inside its own sixth, no crossing cells, generous warm-grey neutral negative space; one primary animal per cell, NOT multiple reference views. Tiny ground/water fragments allowed for mechanics, no full landscapes.
ART DIRECTION: original high-fantasy wildlife with meaningful niches and unfamiliar but coherent whole-body anatomy. Connected skull/neck/limbs, functional mixed coverings, credible weight and locomotion. Recognisable biological logic plus one or two clear unusual changes; not familiar Earth animals with extra accessories. Vary heads beyond lizard faces, body plans, coat/skin/feathers/scales, silhouettes, facing and palette. Don't spread a single new motif to all six. No backpacks, dorsal sacks, gratuitous fringe, throat combs, human gear, decorative fungus, copied franchise creature or portable ecosystems. Animals have their own lives.
PAINT: measured traditional oil/acrylic fantasy concept painting, selective broad brushwork, clear masses, varied edge precision, matte living materials and restrained natural colour. No glossy 3D, photo, mascot, toy, cartoon or uniform pore noise. Soft neutral light but not six identical brown palettes.
SCALE: each cell includes exactly ONE TINY plain grey human silhouette at the same depth and ground/water baseline as its animal, solely to establish the specified size. Use true relative height; do not make humans detailed characters. On an aquatic cell a tiny upright scale silhouette sits unobtrusively at the side. All six animals are separate species proposals, not growth stages. Give the largest appropriate mass and support, not arbitrary spikes or roar. The lineups are alternatives for review, not finished scenes or established canon.

No fire magic, lava skin, walking hill, vegetation growing on its body, insect swarm or dinosaur default. Gentle feeding life with an awe-inspiring unfamiliar shape.

6. Shelf wanderer — 30 m long · cold continental-shelf swimmer. Invent freely a very rare huge cold-water swimmer that migrates over a continental shelf and feeds on seasonal shoals of small animals. Thirty metres long, full silhouette readable, choose an original buoyancy/propulsion/body plan and compact feeding anatomy. No copied whale, serpent, giant fish, jaw curtain, external throat-comb, drifting island or decorative tentacle forest. Real animal logic, subtle beauty and enormous mass.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Revise this ORIGINAL six-creature exploration lineup, 1536 x 1024 landscape, retaining the exact three-column/two-row arrangement with ONE WHOLE animal per cell and no text or borders. Preserve the top-left six-legged land browser and top-right tall low-headed woolly grazer; preserve their faces, coat transitions and anatomical identities. Keep measured broad oil/acrylic brushwork, neutral background and coherent body support.
The aquatic animals currently repeat a whale body too much. REPLACE cells 2, 4 and 6 with three sharply distinct coherent bodies:
TOP CENTRE (2), Undertow: a 24-metre-long flattened soft-bodied marine animal, like an immensely broad swimming velvet slug, continuous fleshy tapering body with TWO PAIRS of wide lateral fin lobes. A small ROUND snub feeding head is continuous with the front of the mantle. No vertebrate torso, whale fluke, dolphin face or fish tail. Rich muted deep teal dorsum and pale salmon underside, matte folds; compact mouth beneath the leading end, no fringe, teeth curtain or tentacles. This is a whole bilaterally symmetrical animal with distinct front and rear.
BOTTOM LEFT (4), Tidal gardener: a 20-metre-long, very broad armoured shallow-coast grazer; EIGHT short jointed oar-like walking limbs along a low oval body, SIX large dull olive/ochre overlapping dorsal plates, and a short blunt soft head tucked naturally beneath the forward rim. Wide oval footprint, low profile, no pincers, giant insect waist or whale fins. It plods along the seabed and takes aquatic vegetation with a small ventral mouth. This is an original huge animal, no trees growing on it.
BOTTOM RIGHT (6), Shelf wanderer: a 30-metre-long elongated cold-water swimmer with THREE PAIRS of broad horizontal paddles attached beneath a tapering softly segmented trunk, a broad blunt compact front bearing paired lateral eyes, and small ventral grasping jaws. The back third narrows to a soft pointed tail WITHOUT a whale fluke or vertical fish fin. Deep muted oxblood and indigo-grey covering with a pale underside. Clear smooth muscular body mass, not a dragon, not spiny and not a literal fossil animal. The three paired paddles give an unmistakably different swimming silhouette.
BOTTOM CENTRE (5), Ashland migrant: replace the humped bear-like body with a 14-metre-long tall open-country walker on FOUR long widely spaced jointed legs with heavy broad padded feet. A deep but narrow torso hangs above the legs; long downward-curving neck ends in a broad rounded mammalian soft-lipped head. Smooth pale grey ash-resistant hide, sparse short black bristles along shoulders and belly, plain long tail. It grazes low new shoots while standing high, not a giant giraffe or horse. No antlers, horns, dorsal ornaments, fire magic or plant growth.
Scale figures must be accurate, not arbitrarily tiny: one flat grey 1.75-metre adult at SAME depth as each animal. Top-left shoulder height FIVE metres, person is 35% of shoulder height. Top-right SIX metres at shoulder, person about 29% of shoulder height. Bottom-centre back height FIVE metres, person 35% of back height. Water animals: person height is 7.3% of top-centre animal's full 24m length, 8.75% of bottom-left animal's 20m length, and 5.8% of bottom-right animal's 30m length. Keep figures alongside, not distant perspective. Fit all bodies completely within their cells, tiny optional water/ground context only. No text, labels, measurements, numbers, signatures or borders.
